text:
Dylan Holloway is in a slump where the work is there and the scoresheet is not. He has 3 goals on 5.7 expected, and his last nine games brought none on 3.7 expected. He is shooting 6.5%, against a usual range nearer 12.5%.

The process around him is sound. St. Louis takes 53.8% of the expected goals at five on five when he plays, 6.6 points better than without him, and he has 46 shots in 19 games. His 13 points are short of where his chances would put him, partly because his teammates have also finished below their chances with him on.

That is a big swing from last season, when Evolving-Hockey ranked him 20th among forwards in wins above replacement while noting his results ran ahead of his chances. This year the dice are going the other way, and our wins added has his goals near the bottom of the league for swinging games.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 80th percentile for primary shot assists, so he can help without scoring. Our projection still has him between 50 and 75 points. What to watch: whether the shots keep coming while he waits.
